samples.summary: mergeDropsHeadingMemory ignores whether the merged-in block actually contributes text, so an empty-into-empty merge discards the remembered heading level for nothing
samples.evidence: The predicate only inspects `block` (`type === 'list-item' && headingLevel !== undefined && every inline empty`) — it never looks at `nextBlock`. Its stated justification is that the incoming *body text* must not inherit the level ("A merge appends another block's text into `block`"). But when the next block is itself empty no text arrives, and the memory is still deleted (`applyMergeBlocks` line 293, and the Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2200). Reachable path: bullet a Heading 2, press Enter to get a second empty bullet (applySplitBlock strips headingLevel from the new half, block-helpers.ts:256-258), select-delete the heading's text so the first bullet is empty, then press Delete/forward-delete at its end — TextEditor.handleDelete (text-editor.ts:1984) calls mergeBlocks(first, emptyNext). The result is an empty bulleted block whose restore-to-Heading-2 intent is silently gone; typing text and un-listing now yields a paragraph. Gating on `getBlockTextLength(nextBlock) > 0` as well would match the documented rationale.

samples.summary: Range-delete that starts at offset 0 of a bulleted heading now silently loses the heading memory via the new merge rule
samples.evidence: deleteSelection deletes the tail of the first block (line 3317-3319) and then merges the last block into it (line 3334). When the selection starts at offset 0 of a bulleted heading, the first block is empty at merge time, so the new predicate fires and `headingLevel` is dropped from both cache and CRDT. In Google Docs the first block's style wins a cross-block delete, so after this change selecting from the start of a bulleted Heading 2 into the following bullet and pressing Delete permanently downgrades the block: un-listing afterwards yields a paragraph rather than the Heading 2 the user bulleted. This path is not covered by any of the new tests (they only exercise Backspace-merge).

samples.summary: dropHeadingMemory is decided from the cached block while the surrounding code explicitly distrusts the cache's view of the tree's inlines
samples.evidence: `const dropHeadingMemory = mergeDropsHeadingMemory(firstBlock);` reads `firstBlock` from the cached document, yet ten lines later the code comments 'Read inline count from the actual tree, not the cache, because previous split/merge operations can leave the tree with a different number of inline nodes than the cache (e.g. split fragments)' (line 2202-2204). If the tree can hold inline nodes the cache does not mirror, the emptiness test can disagree with the tree, and the `removeStyleByPath` at line 2200 would strip `headingLevel` from a tree block that still holds text (or skip a block that does not), leaving the CRDT and the cache — and remote peers — disagreeing about the block's remembered level. Deciding the flag from the tree node's inline text (as the inline-count read does) would remove the doubt.

finding.summary: Remembered headingLevel survives a block merge, so a bullet that now holds only body text can un-list into a heading
finding.evidence: `applyMergeBlocks` (block-helpers.ts:271) returns `cloneBlock(block)` for the surviving block, keeping every attribute including the new `headingLevel` memory; the Yorkie merge path likewise keeps the first node's attributes. Sequence: bullet a Heading 2 (block now `list-item` + `headingLevel: 2`), delete its text, then Backspace at the start of the following plain bullet (`Doc.deleteBackward` -> `mergeBlocks`, document.ts:289). The merged bullet now contains only the *following* item's body text but still remembers level 2, so `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:340) turns that body text into a Heading 2 on the next Enter/Backspace/toggle exit. The new test file explicitly guards the symmetric split direction ('the memory belongs to the block that was bulleted', list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts) but nothing clears the memory on merge.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `applyMergeBlocks` does not simply return `cloneBlock(block)` with all attributes: block-helpers.ts:293 calls `if (mergeDropsHeadingMemory(merged)) delete merged.headingLevel;` before concatenating inlines, and `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (block-helpers.ts:279-285) is true precisely for a `list-item` with a defined `headingLevel` whose inlines are all empty — the exact state the finding's repro produces (bullet a Heading 2, delete its text). The Yorkie path is likewise not unguarded: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2187 computes `dropHeadingMemory = mergeDropsHeadingMemory(firstBlock)` and yorkie-doc-store.ts:2197-2201 removes the `headingLevel` style from the tree inside the same `doc.update`, with the cache updated via `applyMergeBlocks` at :2240. The named reachable path (`Doc.deleteBackward` -> document.ts:289 `mergeBlocks` -> document.ts:349 `store.mergeBlock`) funnels into exactly these two implementations, so no call site reaches the merge without the drop. (document.ts:264-269 further intercepts Backspace in an empty list-item and exits via `unlistedBlockType` instead of merging.) Consequently `unlistedBlockType` (model/types.ts:340) sees `headingLevel === undefined` on the merged block and yields a paragraph, not a Heading 2.
